ppi_focus: Rear differential mounting ears and trunk-floor spot welds inspected from both above (carpet out) and below on a lift, with photographs of every weld; this is pass/fail on a Z3 M.
Rear subframe mounting points, trailing-arm bushings and rear shock mounts / turrets for cracking or deformation.
Cooling system pressure test cold and hot; inspect radiator neck, expansion tank seams, water pump weep hole, thermostat housing and all hose dates for original plastics.
S52 valve-cover gasket and oil filter housing gasket for leaks; check for VANOS rattle at idle and under load.
Tire date codes on all four plus the spare, and confirm matching brand/model and correct staggered sizing.
Clutch engagement point and driveline slack; check motor and transmission mounts, and the finned differential mount.
Convertible top full cycle, frame condition, rear window clarity, drain channels and evidence of water intrusion in the footwells or behind the seats.

Rocker panels, floors, jacking points and the area under the battery tray for corrosion consistent with Midwest winters.
Compression or leak-down on the S52 given long periods of apparent inactivity, and inspect brake fluid, coolant and oil condition.

This 2006 Porsche Cayman S remained in the care of its original owner in California until it was acquired by its current owner on BaT in October 2022. Finished in Lapis Blue Metallic over Stone Gray leather, the car is powered by a 3.4-liter flat-six paired with a six-speed manual transaxle. It rides on 18″ Cayman S wheels and is further equipped with the Preferred Package Plus, a deployable rear spoiler, bi-xenon headlights, heated power-adjustable seats, a Bose sound system, a remote CD changer, air conditioning, and a Becker-Porsche CDR24 head unit. Now with 64k miles, this 987.1 Cayman S is offered on dealer consignment with service records, a Porsche Certificate of Authenticity, a clean Carfax report, and a clean California title.
The car is finished in Lapis Blue Metallic (M5W) and features bi-xenon headlights, fog lights, quarter-panel intakes, a speed-dependent rear spoiler, and dual exhaust outlets. An accident under prior ownership resulted in replacement of the front hood and bumper cover. Separate damage to the lower left quarter panel was also repaired, and related invoices are shown in the gallery below. Photos of paint-meter readings are viewable in the gallery below.
Silver-finished 18” Cayman S wheels are wrapped in 235/40 front and 265/40 rear Michelin Pilot Sport 4S tires with a mixture of 2021 and 2022 date codes. The car is equipped with Porsche Stability Management, and braking is handled by four-piston Porsche-branded calipers over cross-drilled rotors measuring 12.5″ and 11.8″ front and rear, respectively.
The cabin features heated power-adjustable seats upholstered in Stone Gray leather along with a color-coordinated dashboard and carpets. Amenities include a Becker-Porsche CDR24 CD stereo, a Bose sound system, a remote six-disc CD changer, air conditioning, and cruise control.
The leather-wrapped steering wheel frames a central 8k-rpm tachometer, a 190-mph speedometer, and gauges for fuel level and coolant temperature. The digital odometer indicates 64k miles, approximately 1k of which have been added under current ownership.
The mid-mounted 3.4-liter flat-six is located ahead of the rear cargo area and was factory rated at 295 horsepower and 251 lb-ft of torque. Service in 2026 included changing the oil and replacing the ignition coils and spark plugs. The vehicle passed a California emissions test in preparation for the sale.
Power is sent to the rear wheels via a six-speed manual transaxle.
The Porsche Certificate of Authenticity lists factory colors, optional equipment, and a production completion date of June 14, 2006.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are excellent: VIN corroborated three ways, Porsche Certificate of Authenticity confirming Lapis Blue/Stone Gray and factory options, Carfax snapshot, BaT sale history including the $28,000 October 2022 result, named dealer, $0 additional dealer charges, and a stated auction close. Maintenance and condition evidence is genuinely present but thin at the top end: three dated invoices 2024-2026, a VIN-matched DME over-rev scan, a 2011 accident repair order, paint-meter photos in the gallery, and an in-house checklist. What is missing is the expensive half — no borescope, no cooling/AOS/water-pump history, nothing documenting the first 17 years and 62,000 miles beyond the claim that records from new exist, and no follow-up invoice proving the May 2026 misfire was cured. Two internal conflicts (brake and tire measurements) also undercut the dealer checklist's reliability.

condition.rationale: Presentation is strong: paint in the photos looks deep and consistent across panels, panel gaps at the hood and decklid look even, the 18in wheels are unkerbed with matching Michelin PS4S on all four corners, the Stone Gray seats show no bolster collapse or cracking, and the underbody photo shows clean, uncorroded trays, arms and exhaust with no staining around the engine undertray. Against that: a documented cylinder 1/3 misfire four months before the sale with no documented verification of the fix, a car that has covered roughly 1,000 miles in four years (seals, AOS diaphragm, tires and fluids age regardless), brake pads flagged at 4mm to sensor in February 2026 and unexplainedly reported at 7/6mm in August, and no independent assessment of the single most expensive failure mode on this engine. Unknown cylinder-wall condition pulls this down hard on an M97 3.4.

price_value.rationale: The $5,105 shown is an opening-week bid with four bids and six days left, not a market signal. Comparable 987.1 S manuals are settling at $23,250 (2006, 103,700 mi, CA), $27,750 (2007, 97,700 mi), $29,500 (2007, 40,000 mi, San Jose) and up, with a 28,000-mile car failing to meet reserve at $27,500; asking prices on dealer cars run $26,000-$42,000. This car's 64k miles and rare-ish colour combination sit in the upper half of that band, but a disclosed 2011 airbag-deployment accident, an undocumented cooling/AOS history and no borescope are exactly the things that should be priced as a discount, not paid for. It sold for $28,000 here in October 2022 and has gained 1,000 miles and a misfire repair since. Anything in the upper 20s is paying a scope-verified price for an unscoped car.

mission_fit.rationale: As a future keeper the shape is right: a numbers-matching-spec manual 987.1 Cayman S in a desirable colour with a clean over-rev report is a car to own for a decade. But the profile is explicit that a 3.4 S is bought ONLY with unusually strong engine due diligence, and the single mandatory item is absent. It is also the wrong instrument for the immediate problem — it does not relieve the 335i situation cheaply, and a high-20s purchase plus a Porsche-specialist maintenance budget conflicts with the cash-preservation posture implied by accelerated_bridge mode. This is attractive only as a keeper, and only if the scope comes back clean.

logistics.rationale: Modesto is roughly a two-and-a-half-hour drive from Carmel — a same-day round trip with no flight or transport needed. It is a California car with a fresh passed emissions test and all OBD monitors ready, so registration is trivial. The dealer answered questions within hours, ran the DME report on request, posted extra receipts, and explicitly offered local viewing and additional photos or video; the car is stored indoors on a tender. The only constraint is the calendar: an independent Porsche-specialist borescope has to be booked and completed before 10:56am Pacific on September 17, and the dealer has not yet agreed to release the car for an outside PPI.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Lapis Blue Metallic over Stone Gray with the Preferred Package Plus, bi-xenons, heated seats and the deployable spoiler is a genuinely handsome, well-optioned 987.1 — and the photos back it up, with red calipers behind clean silver 18s and an unfussy stock stance. A six-speed manual mid-engined Porsche coupe is squarely in the enthusiast brief and far more special than the MINI/GTI bridge candidates. Only the documented accident history, however minor and however honestly disclosed, keeps this from a 10 for a car intended to be kept.

evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper this is the right car in the wrong evidentiary state: a manual 987.1 Cayman S in Lapis Blue with a clean over-rev report is exactly what the keeper brief describes, but the profile is unambiguous that no borescope means no Cayman S, and nobody — original owner included — has ever looked. It also does nothing for the accelerated_bridge problem and, at a likely high-20s hammer plus Porsche-specialist upkeep, works against the cash-preservation posture the 335i replacement calls for.
evidence.rationale: Hard gate unmet: there is no borescope on this 3.4 M97, and the original owner states in the comments that he never had one done, resting instead on no smoke and no oil consumption — precisely the symptom-based reassurance that counts as zero evidence here. Everything else about the car is better than average. The VIN-matched Autel DME scan is a genuinely good result (Ranges 4-6 all zero, one Range-3 stamp roughly 877 operating hours ago out of 1,827 total), the seller volunteered the 2011 accident that Carfax does not show and published the repair order, and three independent-shop invoices corroborate the odometer chain from 63,018 to 63,630. But those same invoices show what is absent: no water pump, no AOS, no coolant pipes, no clutch, nothing before 2024 despite the claim of records from new. They also show a cylinder 1 and 3 misfire diagnosed on 09 May 2026, four months before the auction, fixed with a camshaft solenoid, sensor, six coils and plugs, with no document proving it stayed fixed — and that sits uncomfortably beside a seller who writes that no work was needed. The dealer's own checklist contradicts the February invoice on both brake pads (7/6mm versus 4mm to sensor) and tires after some 400 miles, which weakens the one inspection on offer. Comps put good 987.1 S manuals between $23,250 and $29,500, so the current $5,105 is an opening bid and nothing more. Logistics are excellent — Modesto is a short drive, the smog is fresh, the seller is responsive — which is exactly why the borescope should be booked rather than the risk accepted.

Underside looks dry and unmolested. Pulling it down: a reported June 2012 damage event with no repair detail, an unknown radiator, unknown AVS/air-bag health, and no cluster or scan evidence. Low mileage does not substitute for the 20-year-old rubber, plastics and driveline fluids.

price_value.rationale: At the captured $15,888 bid this would be a bargain against comps (a 129k-mile 2008 sold for $24,000 on BaT; a 154k-mile 2006 brought $16,500), because 90k miles with Sport/KDSS and a fresh belt is the rare end of the market. But it is a no-reserve BaT auction with 444 watchers and five days left, and the realistic hammer plus BaT fee sits near the upper part of the buyer's price band, before the usual 20-year-old catch-up. Price discipline, not enthusiasm, has to set the bid cap.

mission_fit.rationale: This is the utility_capability branch done properly: body-on-frame V8, dual-range transfer case, Torsen center diff, KDSS articulation, receiver hitch, factory roof rack for a rooftop tent, third row and real dog/gear space — capability the unibody RX 350 does not supply. The overlap caution is real (it is a second big Lexus SUV), so it only earns its place if the off-pavement/tow/rack capability is genuinely wanted. It does nothing for the enthusiast manual brief and should not be counted against that list.

logistics.rationale: Belmont, CA is roughly a 90-mile drive from Carmel — an easy pre-bid inspection and an easy drive home, no transport needed. Toyota/Lexus mechanical is exactly what his mechanic recommends. California-registered since new, so smog and registration are routine. The only constraint is the auction clock: any PPI must be booked inside the five days before the 1:05 pm Pacific close on September 16.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Titanium Metallic over gray leather with the rarer dark Sport wood is a tasteful, unmodified, one-owner Bay Area truck with genuine character as a body-on-frame Land Cruiser Prado relative. It is an automatic SUV, however, and makes no claim on the manual enthusiast brief — the appeal here is competence and adventure utility, not driving reward.

positives: 90k miles on a one-owner, California-since-new GX470 with the timing belt and water pump stated done in March 2026 at ~86k — the single biggest GX price driver addressed.
Sport Package with KDSS, dual-range transfer case, Torsen center diff, receiver hitch and factory roof rack: real capability plus rooftop-tent mounting the RX 350 cannot offer.
Photos show a stock, level, unmodified truck with matching Michelin Defender LTX M/S 2 tires and a dry, patina-only underbody consistent with a lifelong California car.
OEM dashboard replaced with a receipt stated to exist, 2025 battery, ceramic coating applied — the common cracked-dash annoyance is already solved.
Cooperative dealer answering questions in detail, no reserve, $0 additional dealer charges, free Carfax and paint-meter readings published, and the car sits ~90 miles from Carmel.
concerns: Observed: Carfax reports damage in June 2012 and the seller published paint-meter readings, so refinish exists somewhere on the body; no repair invoices or severity detail are provided.
Observed: it is a no-reserve BaT auction with heavy watcher interest and five days left, so the final price is unknown and could land well above the current bid — a hard bid cap is required.
Unverified: the timing-belt/water-pump service is described and a shop is named but no dated invoice is shown (ask Willard's Auto Repair for the itemised receipt showing date, mileage and parts).
Unverified: rear height-control air bags, compressor and AVS status (request a video or PPI showing the truck raising and lowering through all heights and a scan for AVS/ABS codes).
Unverified: original plastic-tank radiator age — no replacement record; on a 20-year-old GX this is a known failure item (ask whether the radiator was replaced with the water pump).
Unverified: transfer case, front/rear differential and transmission fluid service history, plus tire date codes; a 90k-mile car can still be 20 years old on every fluid and rubber item.
unknowns: Extent, location and quality of the repair behind the June 2012 damage entry; which panels the paint meter shows as refinished.
Dated invoice for the timing belt/water pump and whether idlers, tensioner, thermostat and seals were included.

Current California smog certification status for the transfer.
seller_questions: Can you post or email the Willard's Auto Repair invoice for the March 2026 timing-belt service showing date, mileage, and whether tensioner, idlers, thermostat, cam/crank seals and the radiator were included?
Was the radiator replaced at any point, and if so when and with what part? If not, is it the original plastic-tank unit?
Will you allow an independent PPI (my choice of shop, Bay Area) before the auction closes, and can it be scheduled this week?
Please provide the Carfax damage entry detail from June 2012 and any body-shop invoice or estimate from that repair.
Which panels do the paint-meter readings show as refinished, and what are the highest readings recorded?
Can you post a cold-start video with the instrument cluster visible for the first 30 seconds, plus an idle-to-warm shot of the temperature gauge?
Can you post an OBD-II scan report (all modules, including ABS/AVS) showing stored and pending codes?
What are the DOT date codes on all four Michelin Defender tires?
Do you have records for transfer-case, front/rear differential and transmission fluid services, and at what mileages?
Has the rear air-suspension been serviced — any bag, compressor, height sensor or dryer replacement — and will you video the truck cycling through low/normal/high?
Can you photograph the rear frame rails, hitch mounting area and both lower ball-joint boots on a lift?
Is there a current California smog certificate, and will the sale include it?
ppi_focus: Verify the timing-belt job physically: inspect the belt covers/fasteners for recent service marks, check for coolant weep at the water pump and confirm thermostat/seal condition.
Radiator and cooling system: pressure test, inspect the plastic tank seams and transmission cooler for the known GX failure mode.
Rear air suspension: cycle all height settings, check bags for cracking, listen for a labouring compressor, and scan for AVS/height-control codes.
Lower ball joints (recall history) — check for play and boot integrity; also check upper control arm bushings and steering rack for weep.
Exhaust manifolds: listen at cold start for the classic 2UZ tick/crack.
Body repair survey: paint depth readings on every panel, panel gaps, seam sealer and inner-structure inspection to locate the 2012 damage repair.
Frame and underbody on a lift: rails, crossmembers, hitch mounts, rear shackle area — confirm the light patina seen in photos is the whole story.
Fluid condition and analysis: transmission, transfer case, front/rear diffs, brake fluid, coolant condition.
Full OBD scan of all modules plus a highway drive for transmission shift quality, KDSS behaviour and brake pulsation.
Tire DOT date codes and even wear pattern; confirm alignment and no tow-related rear-end abuse.
what_would_change_verdict: A photographed Willard's invoice showing the timing belt, water pump and related parts with date and mileage, plus a clean all-module scan, would move documentation and condition materially upward.
A body-shop record or a clean paint-meter/structural PPI showing the 2012 damage was cosmetic and properly repaired would remove the largest open risk.
Evidence of a sagging rear air suspension, an AVS/check-engine light, a weeping radiator or frame damage found at PPI would drop this well down the list.

A hammer price that pushes the all-in past the buyer's comfortable band for a 20-year-old truck that overlaps the RX 350 would turn a good buy into a poor one; disciplined bidding is the deciding variable.
evidence.mission_note: This satisfies the utility_capability brief on its own merits — body-on-frame V8, low-range, KDSS articulation, hitch, roof rack for a rooftop tent and third-row/dog space that the unibody RX 350 does not provide — and it is a Lexus, which is exactly what his mechanic endorses. It is not a bridge for the enthusiast manual brief; buy it only if the off-pavement and load capability itself is wanted alongside the RX, and bid to a fixed cap given the no-reserve format.
evidence.rationale: This is the strongest GX470 the tracker has seen in this branch: one California owner from new to 2026, 90k indicated miles, Sport Package with KDSS, stock presentation in every attached photo, and a dry, patina-only underbody that reads as a genuine West Coast truck. The two items that price a GX — timing belt and rear suspension — are partly answered: the belt and water pump are stated done in March 2026 at ~86k by a named San Jose shop, and the ride height is level with no lift or aftermarket parts visible, but neither is backed by an invoice or scan reproduced in the listing text. The OEM dashboard was replaced with a receipt said to exist, the battery is 2025, and the tires are matching Michelin Defender LTX M/S 2 with good depth, though date codes are unestablished. Against that, the Carfax shows a June 2012 damage entry and the seller has published paint-meter readings, which is commendable disclosure but not the same as repair documentation — the extent and quality of that work is the biggest open question. The radiator, transfer case, diff and transmission fluids have no records, which is the standard 20-year catch-up rather than a defect. Logistics are near-ideal: Belmont is a short drive from Carmel, PPI before the September 16 close is practical, smog is routine, and BaT shipping is unnecessary. The real risk here is price, not the car: comparable but higher-mileage examples sold from $10,251 to $24,000, and a no-reserve 90k-mile Sport with 444 watchers should be expected to finish near the top of that range. Set a cap, get the belt invoice and a lift inspection first, then bid.
evidence.next_action: Book an independent pre-bid PPI at a Bay Area Toyota/Lexus specialist for this week and simultaneously ask the dealer to email the Willard's Auto Repair timing-belt invoice and a full-module OBD scan before the September 16 1:05 pm Pacific close.

documentation.rationale: Carfax is included and BaT provenance is traceable (sold to this seller 4/20/2024 for $11,000), and specific recent work is named with dates: clutch and hydraulics July 2024, plugs and coils September 2024, brakes 2025. But the seller himself calls the records 'partial,' the April 2019 front/right-front damage has no repair documentation, the ECU tune has no brand/dyno/file provenance, and the two model-critical files — cooling and oil leaks — are entirely absent.

condition.rationale: Real positives: fresh clutch, fresh brakes, new coils and plugs, rear shock mounts done, Bilstein/Eibach suspension. Against that, the listing itself discloses a service brake light that is often on and has never been diagnosed, a torn driver's seat bolster, bumper-cover paintwork over a Carfax damage entry, tired door weatherstripping, weak hood struts, and 'rust visible on underside components' — the underside photo shows heavy surface corrosion on rear suspension hardware typical of a Midwest car. Cooling and oil-leak condition are unexamined, which pulls this down further.

price_value.rationale: No reserve with a $1,750 opening bid and seven days to run; the only comp given is a 2012 Sport with 57k miles at $15,500 (Cars & Bids, April 2026), and this car sold for $11,000 in April 2024 with 13k fewer miles, before the tune/intake/exhaust were a resale question and before the accident-free premium mattered. A realistic landing zone in the high-$8k to low-$12k range would sit at or below the $10-13k target, but the tune, the Midwest underside, five prior owners, and the disclosed damage entry all compress resale in 6-24 months — the thing the mission explicitly cares about.

mission_fit.rationale: On paper this is the exact profile car: manual N52 128i coupe, deliberately chosen by the seller over the turbo 135i for the same reason Jason is leaving the 335i. It fails the 'stock powertrain' half of the brief — aftermarket ECU tune plus intake — and appears not to be a Sport/M Sport car. Add a live brake warning lamp and an undocumented cooling system and it is a bridge that needs work before it is trustworthy, not a turn-key one.

logistics.rationale: Quincy, IL is a long fly-and-drive from Carmel and that is purely a cost item — roughly $1,200-$2,000 in transport or a two-and-a-half day drive Jason has said he will do. The real logistics issue is timing: a PPI must be booked and completed before the 9/13 close, PPI access is not addressed in the listing, and BaT payment moves fast. California registration with a tuned DME and non-CARB intake is an extra step that needs the stock file and stock intake to exist.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Montego Blue over black with a manual, sunroof, no nav screen, Bilstein/Eibach and a strut brace is a genuinely appealing E82 spec, and the shape looks clean and well-kept in the photos. It loses points for leatherette rather than sport seats, the apparent lack of the Sport package Jason's profile asks for, and a modification set that reads as previous-owner taste rather than a factory point of view.

ppi_focus: Cooling system: pressure-test the expansion tank and hoses cold, verify electric water pump operation and coolant temperature control under load, and check pump/thermostat part date stamps
Oil leaks: inspect oil-filter-housing gasket, valve-cover gasket and oil-pan gasket on a lift after degrease, and check the alternator bracket area for oil contamination
Full fault-code scan of all modules with attention to the brake module (the disclosed service brake light) and DME adaptations reflecting the tune
Underside corrosion survey: rear subframe mounting points, trailing-arm bushings, brake and fuel lines, exhaust hangers, and whether fasteners are seizing
Front and right-front structure: check radiator support, inner fender, headlight mounts and bumper reinforcement for the April 2019 damage, plus paint depth readings on all panels
Clutch and manual gearbox: engagement point, pedal feel, no shudder, verify July 2024 work quality and check for rear-main or gearbox seal seepage
Suspension: condition of the Bilstein/Eibach setup, front control-arm bushings and rear shock mounts, plus ride height and any bind from the aftermarket springs
Valvetronic/VANOS operation and cold-start noise on the N52; verify no lifter tick or eccentric shaft sensor codes
Tire date codes, tread depth, and confirmation all four match
Verify open recall status at a BMW dealer, especially the PCV heater and airbag inflator campaigns
what_would_change_verdict: Receipts showing the electric water pump, thermostat and expansion tank replaced within the last few years would remove the largest unknown and move this up materially.

A clean independent PPI on a lift confirming no oil-filter-housing or pan leaks, sound structure at the right front, and surface-only underside rust would justify bidding to the low end of the expected range.
The seller including the stock DME file and factory intake — making a return to CARB-legal configuration a same-day job — would resolve the California registration risk and the resale drag.
A scan proving the brake lamp is a simple wear sensor, with a quote to fix, would convert an open fault into a $200 line item.
If no PPI can be arranged before the 9/13 close, or if the scan shows cooling/oil-leak codes or structural repair at the right front, walk away regardless of price.
evidence.mission_note: This is the right shape of car for the enthusiast-bridge mission — manual, naturally aspirated N52, rear-drive, cheap to exit — and at no reserve it should land inside the $10-13k target. But the tune plus intake, an undiagnosed brake warning light, an undocumented cooling system and a salted Midwest underside make it a project-adjacent bridge rather than a turn-key one, and in accelerated_bridge mode that matters.
evidence.rationale: The result is a conditional yes only with a lift-based PPI and cooling documentation before the 9/13 close. The mechanicals that usually kill these cars have partly been addressed and dated: clutch and hydraulics July 2024, coils and plugs September 2024, brakes 2025, rear shock mounts under prior ownership — and the seller specifically bought an N52 to avoid turbo complexity, the same logic driving Jason away from the 335i. Against that, the listing itself discloses an undiagnosed service brake lamp that is 'often on,' a Carfax front/right-front damage entry from April 2019 with no repair documentation plus bumper-cover paintwork, a torn driver's seat bolster, and 'rust visible on underside components' that the underside photo confirms as heavy surface corrosion on the rear suspension hardware. The two model-critical files — electric water pump/thermostat/expansion tank history and oil-filter-housing/valve-cover/pan leak status — are entirely absent, and a pre-sale oil change makes visual leak assessment harder, so both must be treated as unknown and budgeted. The aftermarket ECU tune and intake break the profile's stock-powertrain requirement, create a California smog and registration step, and will cost money on resale in the 6-24 month window the mission cares about. Provenance is at least honest and traceable: same car, $11,000 on BaT in April 2024, 13k miles ago. At no reserve with $1,750 bid and a week to run, the price should stay in range, but the all-in should be figured with roughly $1,100-$3,200 of known work plus transport from Quincy, IL on top of the hammer.
evidence.next_action: Before bidding, book an independent BMW specialist near Quincy, IL for a lift PPI plus full module scan this week, and ask the seller in the comments for cooling-system receipts and confirmation that a stock DME file and factory intake come with the car.

This 2010 Porsche Cayman S spent a decade in Kentucky, moved to Maryland in 2020, and was acquired by the seller in 2022. Finished in Arctic Silver Metallic over black leather, it is powered by a 3.4-liter flat-six mated to a seven-speed PDK automatic transaxle with a limited-slip differential. Features include the Sport Chrono Package, aftermarket catalytic converters, a modified sport exhaust system, an aftermarket exhaust valve controller, Soul X-pipe exhaust tips, Tarett Engineering rear toe control arms, Bilstein PSS9 coilvers, Frozen slotted rotors, Hawk pads, 18″ alloy wheels, a deployable rear spoiler, power-adjustable seats, air conditioning, a harness bar, and a Pioneer touchscreen infotainment. Work performed in 2022 reportedly included a PDK service as well as replacing the air filter and spark plugs. This 987.2 Cayman S has 83k miles and is offered with a clean Carfax report and a South Carolina title in the seller’s name.
The body is finished in Arctic Silver Metallic (92U). Exterior details include fog lights, a front tow hook, quarter-panel intakes, a speed-dependent rear spoiler, and dual exhaust outlets.
The 18″ Cayman S II wheels are mounted with Michelin and Continental tires. The car is equipped with Porsche Stability Management, and the suspension is modified with Tarett Engineering rear toe control arms and adjustable Bilstein PSS9 coilovers. Braking is handled by red four-piston Porsche-branded calipers loaded with Hawk HP Plus pads over Frozen cross-drilled and ventilated rotors.
The power-adjustable seats are trimmed in black leather. Appointments include air conditioning, a harness bar, power windows, and a Pioneer touchscreen infotainment system.
The Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel was sourced from a 991 and features paddle shifters and a red centering stripe. Instrumentation consists of a central 8k-rpm tachometer, a 190-mph speedometer, and gauges for fuel level and coolant temperature. The Sport Chrono Package added a stopwatch atop the dash. The digital odometer indicates 83k miles, approximately 8k of which were added under current ownership. The check engine light is illuminated, and the seller tells us the diagnostic trouble code is related to the high-flow catalytic converters.

ppi_focus: Full PIWIS/Durametric scan: all stored and pending codes, overrev ranges 1-6, PDK adaptation values and fault memory, readiness monitors.
Catalyst/exhaust inspection: confirm what is welded where, whether OE manifolds are recoverable, and price the return to CARB-compliant units for California registration.
PDK behaviour: low-speed engagement judder, 1-2 shift delay, clutch-pack adaptation data — the 2022 self-performed service is the only claimed fluid change.
Cooling system: water pump vent hole for weeping, pink crust on the block, expansion tank seam and cap, front radiators and condensers with ducts removed for debris packing and corrosion.
Borescope all six cylinders plus a leakdown, and check the bellhousing and RMS area for oil weep and the AOS for cold-start smoke.
Suspension: PSS9 shock bodies for seal leakage and age, Tarett toe link condition and torque, front lower control arm bushings and top mounts, then a corner-weight-aware four-wheel alignment.
Brakes: measure Frozen rotor thickness and condition, confirm Hawk HP+ pad wear and any heat-cracking or bluing that would indicate track use.
Tire DOT dates and sizes on all four corners; confirm the staggered set is correct for the car.
Track-use forensics: harness bar mounting, seat rail and floor for bolt marks, brake duct evidence, rollbar drill holes, and undertray/diffuser scrapes.
Deployable spoiler mechanism operation and a parasitic-draw test given the model's known ignition switch, immobilizer and door-actuator drains.
what_would_change_verdict: It would move up materially if the seller produced the original manifolds/cats plus a specialist scan showing the only code is catalyst-efficiency, and the winning price left room for the OE catalyst restoration and street pads.

It would move up if a Porsche independent completed a pre-close borescope, leakdown and lift inspection with a clean report, and dated invoices surfaced for the water pump/thermostat and the PDK service.
It would move down further if the scan shows overrevs in ranges 4-6, misfire history, or PDK adaptation near limits — that would confirm the track-hardware inference.
It stays a no regardless if the hammer plus catalyst compliance, pads and tires puts it into the same money as a documented, unmodified manual example.
A manual 987.2 S with a specialist service binder at a similar price would displace this car outright.
evidence.mission_note: This fails the enthusiast_bridge brief on the transmission alone — PDK where a manual is required — and it does not earn the pragmatic_bridge exception, because a welded-in non-CARB catalyst setup with an illuminated CEL makes it neither convenient nor immediately usable in California, and there is no maintenance documentation to support the reliability case. In accelerated_bridge mode Jason should be buying evidence and easy resale, and this is a discount-tier, undocumented, modified car in the model's least differentiated colour combination.
evidence.rationale: This is a discount-tier example of an otherwise excellent model, and the disqualifiers are stated in the listing rather than inferred. The check engine light is on right now, caused by aftermarket high-flow catalytic converters welded into the factory manifold assemblies with no CARB EO; the seller confirms South Carolina has no inspections and that he never pursued a fix, which converts a cosmetic annoyance into a California registration project. It is a PDK where the mission requires a manual, and the profile is explicit that manual commands a widening premium while PDK cars sell slower — bad for the 6-24 month exit. Documentation is close to nil on the half that matters: the seller wrote 'I do not have any other service records,' the 2022 PDK service, plugs and annual oil changes are his own home-shop recollection, and a direct bidder question about the water pump and cooling system produced nothing at 83k miles and 16 years. The hardware set — Bilstein PSS9 coilovers, Tarett rear toe links, harness bar, Hawk HP Plus track pads on slotted rotors — is exactly what the profile flags as track-history signature, and the seller can only vouch for his own four years and 8k miles. Tires are mismatched Michelin front and Continental rear with no DOT dates. The car does present cleanly in the photos, the underside shot of the rear subframe looks dry and undamaged, the seller is candid and responsive, and the DFI 3.4 with LSD and Sport Chrono is genuinely the right engine — but with the auction closing in about a day there is no realistic path to a Porsche-specialist borescope, leakdown and scan before money moves.
evidence.next_action: Do not bid; if Jason wants to stay engaged, post one public question asking whether the original OEM manifolds/cats are included and requesting a photo of the scan tool showing the exact DTC and readiness status, and let the auction close without him unless a specialist PPI can be completed before it ends.

critical_evidence.evidence: Not applicable in the M20 sense: the M42 is chain-driven. The listing states a 'replacement timing set' was installed with the 2022 engine build; no invoice reproduced, and the M42 upper chain guide/tensioner is its own known wear item.

One underbody photo of the rear differential/subframe area shows clean, freshly finished components with only light surface rust on the diff cover; no shock-tower, trunk battery corner, floor pan, jack point or rocker photos provided. Canadian-market car of unknown pre-2016 climate exposure.

documentation.rationale: Real strengths: published VIN, Carfax with 8 service and 44 detailed records, owner's manuals, a photographed records folder, build-bench photos of the forged rotating assembly, and a named tuning shop. But every substantive claim about the build, the clutch, the LSD and the A/C rebuild is 'reportedly/said to be' in listing prose; no invoices, dyno sheet, machine-shop paperwork, compression numbers or 2008 accident repair documentation are reproduced. Long single ownership through the build helps, but for a car whose value rests entirely on build quality, the verifiable layer is thin.

condition.rationale: Presentation is genuinely strong: straight silver panels with even reflections, tidy shutlines, intact sport seat bolsters, an uncracked dash top, and an engine bay that looks assembled with care. Recent hardware is dated and plausible — 2026 brake overhaul (master, calipers, rotors, pads), 2026 tires, 2024 subframe/control arms/wheel bearings, 2024 driveshaft center bearing and CV boots. The single underbody photo is clean and dry. What pulls it down is what is not shown: no shock tower, trunk battery corner or floor photos on a Canadian-market car, no health data on a 2022 built engine (leakdown, coolant temps, oil pressure log), and a documented front-end collision whose inner structure has never been photographed.

price_value.rationale: At the captured $3,600 opening bid it looks cheap, but this is a reserve auction with 258 watchers and a build story; realistic hammer is well into the mid-to-high teens plus 5% buyer fee, which lands above Jason's $15k all-in bridge target and near his ideal band ceiling. Against the peer 1987 325is at $11,000, this is a four-cylinder 318is with a Carfax moderate accident, repainted front clip, a bespoke standalone-managed engine and non-CARB hardware — exactly the profile that the documentation-driven E30 market discounts on resale. You would be paying enthusiast-build money for an asset whose next buyer pool is narrow.

mission_fit.rationale: It clears the manual requirement and it is local and inspectable, but the mission asks for a reliable, easy-to-resell, sub-$15k-all-in bridge with low ownership friction. A 10.5:1 forged M42 on ITBs and a Haltech tune, with a cat-delete pipe and CARB-questionable hardware in a state where Jason must smog it every two years, is the opposite of low friction — and his mechanic does VW/Toyota, not standalone tuning. Resale in 6-24 months depends on finding another E30 build buyer rather than the broad market.

logistics.rationale: San Mateo is roughly 85 miles from Carmel — a same-day drive for a PPI and a drive home. Seller is a private party, publicly responsive, offering additional photos, videos and records, plus a new catalytic converter, the stock airboxes and a current passing California smog certificate to a California buyer. California title in his name, no transport needed. The only logistics friction is the auction clock (closes 2026-09-11) which compresses PPI scheduling.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Sterling Silver over black leatherette, sport seats, sunroof, Alpina-style 16s, M-Technic wheel, LSD and a short shifter is a handsome, coherent E30 coupe that would be a genuine Carmel Valley Road car, and the ITB noise is a real draw. It falls short of the profile's ideal on two counts: it is a 318is four rather than the M20 325is six the buyer's brief describes, and it is a heavily modified car rather than a preserved, documented original — the character is the builder's, not the factory's.

Has the M42 profile gasket ever been replaced, and is there any oil/coolant intermixing or weeping at the block/head seam?
Is the shown 122k km original to the chassis — do you have the Canadian export paperwork and the pre-2016 service history?

ppi_focus: Cylinder leakdown and compression on the built M42, plus cold-start behaviour and oil pressure at hot idle.
Cooling system pressure test and inspection of the M42 profile-gasket seam, radiator, expansion tank and hoses for weeping or intermixing.
Structural check of the repaired front end: paint depth on hood/fenders, radiator support and frame rail alignment, weld and sealant originality behind the fenders.
Rust survey specific to a Canadian car: front shock towers under the strut hats, trunk battery corner, rear subframe and trailing-arm mounting points, floors, jack points, sunroof drains.
Haltech scan and datalog review — fault history, AFR under load, coolant temp, and whether the tune tolerates a catalytic converter and the stock airbox.
Chase Bays braided brake and power-steering line installation quality and DOT-compliance of the fittings, plus master cylinder and pedal feel after the 2026 overhaul.
Drivetrain: 325is LSD lock-up test (one-wheel spin), diff and output seal leaks, driveshaft center bearing vibration at 45-60 mph, clutch engagement and any throwout squeal.
Suspension and steering after the E36 M3 rack conversion: alignment printout, bump steer, poly bushing NVH, ball joints, tie rods and Bilstein damper condition.
Electrical: instrument cluster odometer/OBC operation on the km cluster, A/C output temperature after the claimed rebuild, sunroof operation, LED headlight beam pattern legality.
Emissions dry-run: confirm the car can be presented smog-legal with the supplied cat and stock intake, ideally by taking it to a smog shop as part of the PPI.
what_would_change_verdict: Full build invoices plus a clean leakdown and a Haltech datalog showing normal coolant temps and AFR, combined with lift photos or a specialist PPI confirming no structural damage from the 2008 front hit and no rust — that would move it from a speculative build to a documented one.
A BAR referee certificate (or a smog certificate obtained in the exact configuration the car will be delivered in) that makes California registration a non-issue rather than an open liability.
A hammer price that keeps all-in under about $13,000 including fee and the compliance work — at that number the risk is priced in and it becomes a defensible fun bridge.
Bidding past roughly $16,000 all-in, or a PPI finding poor front-end repair, coolant-temp problems on the built motor, or shock-tower/subframe corrosion — any of those should end it.
Seller declining or slow-walking a pre-auction PPI at an independent Bay Area BMW specialist would make this a pass on principle.
evidence.mission_note: As an enthusiast bridge this is charismatic and geographically ideal but mission-adverse: a forged, standalone-tuned, cat-deleted 318is is a specialist toy that Jason's VW/Toyota mechanic cannot support, that carries an unresolved California emissions question, and that resells to a narrow build-buyer audience rather than quickly. It is not a pragmatic bridge either — the whole point of the bridge is dependable, cheap, easy-to-exit, and this car is none of those three despite looking the part.
evidence.rationale: This is a well-presented, heavily engineered E30 that fails the brief for structural reasons rather than cosmetic ones. The verifiable evidence is decent for a private BaT car — published VIN, Carfax with 8 service and 44 detailed records, build-bench photos, a named tuner, nine years of single ownership, and dated recent work (2026 brakes and tires, 2024 subframe, control arms, wheel bearings, driveshaft center bearing, CV boots) — but the entire value proposition, the 2022 forged 2.0L M42 with Haltech and ITBs, is supported only by seller prose: no invoices, no leakdown, no logs, no machine-shop paperwork. Carfax records an October 2008 moderate front-damage accident and a 2009 damage claim, the hood and front fenders are repainted, and no inner-structure photos or repair documentation exist. The car was a California Gross Polluter in 2021 and currently runs a catalyst-delete pipe with hardware the listing itself admits may not be CARB-certified, which sits in direct tension with the seller's promise of a passing smog certificate. It is a Canadian-market import with no shock-tower, trunk-corner or floor photos, so rust is unknown, not absent. Logistics are excellent — San Mateo, cooperative seller, easy PPI — and the emotional pull is real, but a reserve auction with 258 watchers points to a mid-to-high-teens hammer plus fee, above the sub-$15k all-in bridge target, for an asset that is harder to resell and harder to service than the GTI, F56 or 128i alternatives. Buy only on a clean specialist PPI, full build receipts, and a price that stays cheap.
evidence.next_action: Before bidding, book a pre-auction PPI at an independent Bay Area BMW/standalone-EFI specialist (leakdown, cooling pressure test, Haltech datalog, lift inspection of the repaired front clip and shock towers) and simultaneously ask the seller in the comments for the engine build invoices and the configuration of the December 2024 smog certificate.

what_would_change_verdict: Clear photographs (or a specialist report) showing sound, uncracked trunk-floor spot welds and diff mounting ears — or better, documented reinforcement plates already fitted — would move this from speculative to seriously worth chasing.

Invoices showing a cooling-system refresh (water pump, radiator, expansion tank, thermostat, hoses) within the last few years, plus the itemized Nov 2023/2025 receipts, would lift documentation substantially.
An independent BMW specialist PPI completed before the close, with a clean structural verdict, would justify bidding toward the upper end of the expected range.
Photos showing cracking at the diff mount or trunk-floor welds, or a refusal/failure to produce them before close, would take this off the list at any price above scrap-value bidding.
A hammer price drifting above roughly $16,000 without structural and cooling evidence would defeat the value case entirely — walk at that point.
evidence.mission_note: As a future_keeper this is the right shape of car — factory manual, S52 rather than the rod-bearing S54, LSD, Imola Red, mostly stock — but a keeper is exactly the mission that demands proof of the rear structure and cooling history, and this listing supplies neither. It does nothing for the accelerated_bridge problem either: a 123k-mile roadster with an original-as-far-as-we-know cooling system is not a dependable replacement for the ailing 335i, so buying it would spend cash without solving the actual pressure.
evidence.rationale: This is an appealing, honestly presented, high-mileage M Roadster whose value case currently rests on a $5,750 bid that will not survive two more days. The genuine strengths are structural to the model rather than to this car: the 2000 model year means an S52, so the S54 rod-bearing and double-VANOS liabilities that dominate 2001-02 ownership simply do not apply, and the spec — five-speed, LSD, Imola Red over black Nappa, Style 40 wheels, apparently stock — is on brief. The photos support the cosmetic story: even paint, normal shutlines, clean wheels, a tidy engine bay with no coolant crust, and an underbody free of rust scale. But the single most expensive failure mode on a Z3 M is the trunk-floor and differential-mount weld area, a BaT commenter asked for exactly those photos on day one, and the seller's only reply was that the car would have to go on a lift; nothing has appeared since. Cooling is equally silent — the documented Nov 2025 work covers valve cover and oil pan gaskets, A/C and a heater valve, all oil-and-comfort items, with no radiator, pump, tank or thermostat anywhere in the record, on a 26-year-old car at 123k miles. The listing also establishes two real defects itself: a mismatched Nexen/Sumitomo tire set that must be replaced, and a disclosed shrinking soft-top edge, plus a probable window switch or regulator fault visible to a commenter. The comp evidence says a car like this belongs near the $10,900 Mill Valley 115k-mile result rather than the $20k-$27k low-mileage sales, so there is room to buy well — but only with the structure verified, and the showroom reopens the same morning the auction closes at 10:01am Pacific, which makes a real specialist PPI nearly impossible in the window.
evidence.next_action: Post a public comment today demanding the promised lift photos of the differential mounting ears plus trunk-interior shots of the spot welds with carpet removed, and ask directly whether an independent BMW specialist can lift the car on Tuesday morning 9/8 before the 10:01am Pacific close — bid only if those weld photos come back clean, and cap at roughly $14,000 hammer.

evidence.mission_note: As a body-on-frame V8 with low range and a locking center diff, a GX470 is one of the few SUVs that genuinely adds capability the RX 350 already at home does not, so the mission logic holds. But this specific truck is a five-owner Pennsylvania-titled example with a disputed, coated-over underside and no timing-belt evidence, closing in under a day 2,700 miles away with no inspection window — the model fits the mission far better than this car does.
evidence.rationale: The result is driven by evidence that is almost entirely seller prose. The two items that set GX470 value — timing-belt documentation and rear-suspension status — are both absent: a bidder asked about the belt on Aug 31 and the seller simply never answered, and the AVS/height control appears only as an equipment line. Worse, two separate commenters read the underside photos as undercoating over bubbling corrosion on a truck the listing itself says was last owned in Pennsylvania, and the dealer's rebuttal is three sentences with no close-up photos posted. Frame rust is a hard reject on this profile, and unknown here is not good. The listing does disclose real defects honestly — cracked dash (a $1,700-2,500 job by the comment thread's own estimate) and touched-up roof and bumper covers — and the truck presents well in the photos: straight, stock, tidy engine bay, intact undershields. Price is the strongest argument: $5,000 no-reserve against comps that failed to meet reserve at $11,600 and $15,500 leaves genuine room. But the auction ends in roughly a day in Daytona Beach, which makes this a remote blind purchase on the one question that could cost the whole purchase price, and Arroyo tires of unknown age plus no cooling or driveline service records add to the catch-up pile. Cheap, plausible, and unproven where it matters most.
evidence.next_action: Before the close, hire a local Daytona mobile inspector to probe the frame under the coating and scan the truck, and demand the seller post rear-frame close-ups and any timing-belt receipt; if either the inspection or the frame photos do not happen, do not bid.

Doug's Take
We love the BMW Z3 M Roadster here on Cars & Bids, as it's a fantastic convertible that boasts handsome styling, a mandatory 5-speed manual transmission, and a great soundtrack from its sporty 6-cylinder engine. This particular Z3 M touts some nice factory equipment, including a limited-slip differential, Nappa leather upholstery, and a Harman/Kardon sound system – along with no major modifications. It also comes with recent servicing and mostly warm-climate California ownership since new, which is a great benefit – AND it's offered with the thrill of no reserve!
Highlights

This Z3 M is equipped with a 5-speed manual transmission.

contradictions.detail: Facebook header states 'Driven 192,000 miles' while the seller's own description says '190k miles maintained with care'. Likely rounding, but the two figures in the same ad do not match and no odometer photo is provided.

critical_evidence.evidence: The 2010-2012 GX460 secondary air injection pump/valve failure (P2440/P2442) is the single most expensive known fault on this car and the ad's mechanical list does not mention pumps, valves, codes or a scan. No OBD scan photo attached.

documentation.rationale: Weak on both halves. Identity and terms: no VIN, no odometer photo, no title photo — only a Facebook attribute set (clean title, 2 owners, 192k) and a named private seller with a rating history; the equipment description is detailed and the photos confirm most of it. Maintenance and condition evidence: essentially zero — a bullet list of claimed work (radiator, thermostat, plugs, brakes, filters) with no dates, no mileages, no invoices, no scan, no service history, and no documentation of the suspension install. At 192,000 miles the claim list is the least persuasive form of evidence available.

condition.rationale: Photos genuinely look good: straight panels, consistent grey paint, clean beige leather in all three rows with no bolster collapse or cracked dash, working nav/ML/RSE hardware, matching Falken AT3Ws with real tread, tidy rack and hitch. Against that, this is a 192k-mile first-year GX460 with the three expensive model faults — secondary air injection, KDSS, valley-plate/timing-cover coolant seepage — entirely unaddressed in the ad, plus a lift of unknown install quality on a KDSS chassis, and no underhood, undercarriage or cold-start evidence. Trail photos show the car has actually been used off pavement. Unknowns dominate the areas that cost the most.

price_value.rationale: The asking price is far off the market. A 2010 Premium with 173,709 miles is asking $16,995 in Modesto; a 2010 Premium with 230,000 miles sold for $9,800 in Escondido; a 142,900-mile 2010 sold for $14,250 on Cars & Bids; and a 2017 Premium with 128,500 miles asks $23,900 — the same money as this 2010 with 192,000 miles. Bolt-ons (Ironman kit, rack, AT tires, traction boards) recover pennies on the dollar at resale and, per Jason's brief, add modest value at most. The ad has sat nine weeks at one price with no reduction, which is itself market feedback.

mission_fit.rationale: The capability case is real: body-on-frame, low range, locking centre diff, KDSS, Crawl Control, a full-length roof rack that suits a rooftop tent, a hitch, and a third row — all things the RX 350 cannot supply. But this is also a second large Lexus SUV in the driveway, it is a 192k-mile example rather than a low-risk one, and the mission requires it to justify the overlap on capability and dependability. A cheaper, lower-mileage GX would satisfy the same mission with far less exposure.

logistics.rationale: Mission Viejo is roughly 330 miles from Carmel — a one-day drive or a short flight, and Jason will drive a good car home. Southern California means abundant Toyota/Lexus and GX-specialist shops for a PPI including a KDSS-aware inspection, and the seller has a 20-rating marketplace history. Offsets: PPI access is not addressed in the ad, no VIN is published so nothing can be pre-checked, and a California private-party sale requires the seller to supply a current smog certificate, which is unstated.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Grey over beige with wood trim, Mark Levinson, rear entertainment and a tasteful mild overland build is an attractive, coherent package and photographs well on a fire road. It is also an automatic V8 SUV and makes no claim on the enthusiast brief (MINI/GTI/128i/Z3); its appeal is competence and family utility, not character Jason is chasing.

positives: Genuinely capable spec the RX 350 lacks: KDSS, Crawl Control, low range, full-length roof rack suited to a rooftop tent, hitch and a power third row.
Photographic condition is strong for the mileage — straight panels, consistent grey paint, clean beige leather in all three rows, uncracked dash, intact nav/Mark Levinson/RSE hardware.
Southern California car with a matching set of Falken Wildpeak AT3W all-terrains and a level, modest lift rather than a big cheap one.
Toyota 1UR-FE/J150 platform is exactly what Jason's mechanic recommends and parts/specialist support in California is excellent.
Private seller with a long-standing, highly rated marketplace account within a day's drive, so a specialist PPI before money moves is straightforward to arrange.
concerns: Observed: the price is out of step with the comps — $23,995 for a 192,000-mile 2010 when a 2017 Premium with 128,500 miles asks $23,900 and a 173,709-mile 2010 Premium asks $16,995; it has sat nine weeks with no reduction.
Observed: an Ironman 4x4 lift has been installed over a KDSS chassis with no install invoice, alignment sheet or lean measurement, and the trail photos confirm the truck has been used off pavement.

Observed: every mechanical item is a claim in a bullet list — radiator, thermostat, plugs, brakes — with no date, mileage or receipt behind any of it, and no reason given for the radiator and thermostat replacement.
Unverified: secondary air injection status on a 2010-2012 GX460 (ask for a full OBD scan including stored/pending codes, and any P2440/P2442 history or pump replacement invoice).
Unverified: KDSS leak or cross-corner lean (inspect the valve body, accumulators and sway-bar cylinders for weep and measure lean on level ground).
Unverified: 1UR-FE valley-plate and timing-cover coolant seepage, plus frame and underbody condition (request underhood and undercarriage photos and a lift inspection).
unknowns: VIN — nothing can be decoded, history-reported or recall-checked until it is provided.

Can you send a photo or printout of a full OBD scan showing stored and pending codes plus readiness monitors, taken in the last week?

Have the transmission, transfer case and front/rear differential fluids been changed, and at what mileage?

Do you have a current California smog certificate, and will the sale include one?
What are the DOT date codes on the four Falken tires, and do you have the purchase receipt?
Can you send a cold-start video of at least two minutes, from key-on, with the instrument cluster in frame?
ppi_focus: Secondary air injection: scan for P2440/P2442, check pump operation on cold start and inspect the valves/pump for moisture intrusion.
KDSS: inspect valve body, accumulators and both sway-bar cylinders for hydraulic weep; measure cross-corner lean on level ground and confirm the system still articulates after the lift.
1UR-FE coolant: inspect the valley plate area, timing cover and water pump for seepage; pressure-test the cooling system and check for oil/coolant cross-contamination.
Frame rails, crossmembers and skid areas from below for rust, impact damage or bent components from off-road use.
Lift installation quality: control-arm and shock mounting, CV boot and axle angle, driveshaft/carrier bearing, brake and ABS line routing, and steering geometry/alignment specs.
Transfer case actuator function: shift into 4-Lo and back, confirm no fault codes and no grinding.
Suspension bushings, ball joints, tie rods and rear shocks at 192k miles.
Automatic transmission: fluid condition and level via the check procedure, road-test for shift quality and torque-converter lockup shudder.
Tire DOT date codes and irregular wear pattern that would reveal alignment issues after the lift.
Full body/paint meter check and panel-gap review for unreported collision repair, since no history report exists.
what_would_change_verdict: A clean specialist PPI plus a full scan with no codes, documented healthy KDSS with no lean, and dry valley plate/timing cover — combined with a price renegotiated toward the $15,000-17,000 band the comps support.
Production of dated invoices for the air-injection system, drivetrain fluids and the lift install, converting the claim list into records.
The VIN and a clean history report confirming two owners, no accidents and completed recall work.
Downward: any P2440/P2442 code, visible KDSS hydraulic weep or measurable lean, or coolant seepage at the valley plate — each is four figures on top of an already over-market ask.
Downward: seller declining to release the VIN or to allow a PPI at an independent shop.
evidence.mission_note: This does deliver capability the RX 350 genuinely lacks — body-on-frame, low range, KDSS, roof rack for a rooftop tent, hitch and a third row — so it clears the overlap test on paper. But at 192,000 miles with the three expensive GX460 faults entirely undocumented and an asking price at the level of a 2017 with 64,000 fewer miles, it is not the low-risk capability buy the accelerated_bridge mode calls for at this number.
evidence.rationale: The verdict is driven by price and evidence, not by the truck itself. Condition in the photos is legitimately good: straight grey paint, clean beige leather across three rows, intact Mark Levinson and rear-entertainment hardware, matching Falken AT3Ws and a level, modest lift. But the ad's entire mechanical case is a bullet list — radiator, thermostat, plugs, brakes, filters — with no date, mileage or invoice behind a single line, and at 192,000 miles that is the weakest possible support. Every one of the four model-critical items is missing: no scan for P2440/P2442 secondary air injection, no KDSS leak or lean check on a chassis that has had an Ironman kit installed over it, no underbody or frame images, and no lit-cluster or cold-start evidence. No VIN is published, so no history report, recall check or decode is possible. The market is unambiguous: a 173,709-mile 2010 Premium asks $16,995 in Modesto, a 142,900-mile 2010 sold at $14,250, a 230,000-mile one sold at $9,800, and a 2017 Premium with 128,500 miles asks $23,900 — the same as this. Nine weeks at $23,995 with no reduction confirms the market's read. The build is a modest positive at best under Jason's own rule that accessories never substitute for evidence.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a recent full OBD scan photo (stored and pending codes), the Ironman install invoice with alignment sheet, and confirmation he will meet at a GX/Toyota specialist in Orange County for a lift PPI — and open the price conversation at the $15,000-17,000 the comps support before booking anything.

facts.note: Lift, wheels, tires and roof basket all visible in photos and listed in the ad. No engine or drivetrain modification claimed or visible.

facts.note: Mileages given but no dates, no shop names, no invoices, no photographs of receipts.

Fixed asking price of $14,000 on Facebook Marketplace, not an auction.

contradictions.topic: Model year: listing headline vs. seller description
contradictions.detail: The Facebook listing title reads '2008 Lexus GX 470 Sport Utility 4D' while the seller's first line reads '2007 NOT a 2008!'. Self-corrected by the seller, but the actual year matters for the 2007+ secondary-air-injection issue and for pricing; only a VIN decode settles it.

critical_evidence.evidence: Seller states 'Timing Belt, Water pump, and Radiator replaced at 179k' — 19,500 miles ago on a 90k-mile interval, which would be ideal if true. No date, no shop, no invoice, and no photo of the belt cover or a service sticker.

Eibach Pro-Truck Lift Stage 2R named in the ad; photos show an even, level ride height at all four corners with no rear sag and no obvious cheap spacer-lift geometry. Whether the rear air springs/AHC compressor were retained, replaced, or converted to coils is not stated, and control arms/tie rods/rack were replaced at 142k-173k by claim only.

Seller writes 'No rust'; the car presents as a Southern California vehicle and visible rockers, wheel arches and lower doors look clean in the side photos. No frame, crossmember or undercarriage photo is attached, so the structure was not examined here.

No dash, cluster or scan-tool image in the attached photos and no statement about lights. 'Runs great' is a seller sentence, not a scan; AVS/height-control, ABS/VSC and check-engine status are all unknown.

All four corners photographed showing matching bronze Method wheels with matching 33in BFGoodrich all-terrain tires and deep tread; the ad adds a full-size matching spare on a fifth wheel. DOT date codes are not readable in these images, so age remains a question even though matching and tread are established.

Radiator claimed replaced with the timing belt at 179k, which addresses the known plastic-tank failure mode if documented. No engine-bay photograph, no coolant-reservoir shot, no undercarriage image, and no statement about oil leaks (rear main, timing cover, valve covers) at 198.5k.

documentation.rationale: Split badly between the two halves. Identity and terms are weak-to-middling: named private seller, firm $14,000 price, mileage, colors and a modification list, but NO VIN, no title photo, no history report, and the headline year contradicts the description. Maintenance evidence is the seller's typed list only — eight jobs with mileages but no dates, shops, or a single invoice or receipt photo. The list is specific enough to be credible-sounding, which makes verification more important, not less.

condition.rationale: Photographic evidence is genuinely encouraging as far as it goes: straight black paint with even panel gaps, no visible dents, clean rockers and arches, tidy grey leather with only light bolster sheen, matching deep-tread all-terrains, level stance with no rear sag, and a quality Eibach lift rather than a spacer job. But this is a 198,500-mile body-on-frame Lexus and the attached set contains no engine bay, no undercarriage or frame, no odometer, no cluster, no dashboard top (crack-prone), and no third-row/cargo shot. Headlight lenses are visibly hazed. Unknowns at this mileage pull the number down.

price_value.rationale: $14,000 sits at or slightly above the market this comp set describes: a 176k-mile 2008 asks $15,000 in San Jose, a 195k-mile 2004 SOLD at $13,000 in Oceanside, and a 192k-mile Sport Package car failed to meet reserve at $11,600 on Cars & Bids. The profile is explicit that heavily modified builds trade at a discount to clean stock examples, and 33s plus a lift on 198.5k miles is a modification premium the seller is asking the buyer to pay. The claimed timing belt/water pump/radiator at 179k is worth real money — but only once documented; unpaid-for claims should not be priced as done work.

mission_fit.rationale: For the utility_capability branch this delivers what the RX 350 cannot: body-on-frame construction, full-time 4WD with a locking center diff, a 2UZ V8, a roof basket already mounted for a rooftop tent or gear, and a flat cargo area suited to a sleeping platform. That said, the catch-up note is real — a GX overlaps the RX for family and dog duty, so it only earns its place if the off-pavement and rooftop-tent capability is itself wanted. Fuel consumption at 15 mpg combined and the 33in tires' effect on gearing and ride are the daily costs of that capability.

logistics.rationale: Corona, CA is roughly 300-330 miles from Carmel — an easy fly-or-drive day and a trivially drivable trip home in a functioning GX, and California-legal with no out-of-state registration friction. Toyota/Lexus specialists are plentiful in the Inland Empire, so a PPI should be easy to book, but PPI access, smog certificate status and seller flexibility are all unconfirmed, and no VIN has been released for a pre-trip history pull.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Black over grey with bronze Method wheels, flares and a low-profile roof basket is a tasteful, coherent look rather than a hard-parked overland caricature, and the GX's wood-and-leather cabin still feels like a Lexus. But it is an automatic SUV, not the enthusiast brief — this is explicitly a capability/pragmatic pick, and Jason should not expect it to scratch the MINI/GTI/Z3 itch.

known_work_items: Hazed/yellowed headlight lenses visible in front-three-quarter and head-on photos — restoration or lens replacement
positives: Claimed timing belt, water pump AND radiator all replaced at 179k — the three biggest GX470 money items — leaving roughly 70k miles of belt interval if the receipts exist.

Unusually specific eight-item maintenance narrative from 142k to 179k (control arms, rack and pinion, PS pump, CV axles, tie rods, diff service, front brakes) that fits a genuinely maintained truck rather than a flipped one.
Photos show four matching deep-tread 33in BFGoodrich all-terrains on matching bronze Method wheels plus a full-size matching spare — no mismatched-rubber tax and real trail redundancy.
Level, unsagged stance at all four corners with a quality Eibach Pro-Truck kit rather than a cheap spacer lift; body sits square in both side profiles.
Straight, clean Southern California black paint with even gaps, tidy grey leather, and a roof basket already fitted for the rooftop-tent or gear-hauling camping intent.
300-ish miles from Carmel, California-registered, private seller with a decade-plus profile who corrected his own listing's model year unprompted.
concerns: Observed: the listing headline says 2008 and the description says 2007 — a one-year identity question that also decides whether the 2007+ secondary-air-injection system is in play, and there is no VIN in the ad to settle it.

Observed: $14,000 for 198,500 miles with a lift and 33s sits above a 195k-mile GX that SOLD at $13,000 in Oceanside and a 192k-mile Sport that could not clear $11,600 at auction; the modifications are being priced as value when the profile says they trade at a discount.
Observed: headlight lenses are visibly hazed/yellowed in the front photos — cheap to fix but it is real, established work.

Unverified: every one of the eight claimed repairs, including the timing belt/water pump/radiator at 179k, is a typed sentence with no date, shop or invoice (ask for photographs of all receipts and the belt-service sticker).

Unverified: rear air-spring / height-control status is never mentioned despite a lift being installed — bags could be original at 198.5k, could be delete-converted, could be masked (ask directly and inspect the compressor, bags and AVS lamp).
Unverified: no scan data, no cluster photo and no engine-bay or undercarriage image, so warning lights, oil leaks, exhaust manifold tick and frame condition are all unexamined at nearly 200k miles.
unknowns: VIN — blocks year confirmation, title/accident history, recall status (lower ball joint campaign) and any odometer cross-check.
Whether the rear air suspension bags/compressor are original, replaced, or converted to coils, and whether the AVS/height-control lamp is off.
OBD-II scan results and cluster condition: check engine, VSC/ABS, and any stored codes.
Frame, crossmember and skid-plate condition underneath; the 'no rust' claim has no photo behind it.
Dates on the claimed services — mileage without dates hides how long fluid-sensitive work has been sitting.
Tire DOT date codes; deep tread does not rule out aged rubber on a lifted truck.
Transmission and transfer-case service history — the ad lists a diff service at 173k but no transmission fluid work at any point.
Current smog certificate status and registration currency.
Dashboard-top condition (known GX cracking) and third-row presence/condition.
How long the seller has owned it and whether the pre-142k history is available.
seller_questions: Can you send the VIN so I can pull the history report and confirm the 2007 build year before I drive down?
Can you photograph the actual invoices for the timing belt, water pump and radiator at 179k — I need the shop name and the calendar date, not just the mileage.
Were the rear air suspension bags and the height-control compressor replaced, or converted to coil springs, and at what mileage? If original, do they hold overnight?
Can you send a photo of the instrument cluster with the engine running, and an OBD-II scan screenshot showing no stored or pending codes?
Has the transmission fluid or the transfer case fluid ever been serviced? Your list shows a diff service at 173k but nothing for the trans.
Can you send photos of the frame rails, rear crossmember and the underside of the floor pan taken from underneath, plus one of the engine bay?
What are the DOT date codes on the four BFGs and the spare (the four-digit number on the sidewall)?
Does the truck have a current California smog certificate, and is registration current through what date?
Any oil leaks you're aware of — valve covers, timing cover, rear main — and is there any exhaust manifold tick on a cold start?
Can you send a cold-start video, engine off overnight, showing the first 60 seconds including the dash lights?
Would you allow a pre-purchase inspection at a Toyota/Lexus specialist near Corona, at my expense, before any money moves?
Are the original wheels, tires and any removed stock suspension parts included, and is the third-row seat present?
ppi_focus: Rear air springs, height-control compressor and AVS operation: cycle heights, check for leak-down and for a masked/deleted system behind the Eibach lift.
Verify the timing belt service physically — inspect belt condition and any dated service sticker, check water pump weep hole and the replacement radiator's tanks and hoses.
Full frame and undercarriage inspection: rails, rear crossmember, control-arm mounts and skid plates for corrosion or off-road impact damage.
Lift geometry check: CV axle angles, driveshaft and slip-yoke condition, panhard/track-bar and steering-linkage angles, plus alignment and any tire-edge wear from the 33s.
Lower ball joints (recall history) and steering rack — the rack and PS pump are claimed replaced at 173k, so confirm the parts look recent and dry.
OBD-II scan for stored/pending codes; on a 2007 specifically check the secondary air injection system for pump and valve faults.
Exhaust manifolds for cracks/tick on cold start, and a compression or leak-down check given nearly 200k miles.
Transmission fluid condition and a road test for shift quality, torque-converter shudder and transfer-case center-diff lock engagement.
Paint-depth gauge on all panels and gap check to test the 'no accidents' claim in the absence of a history report.
Dashboard top for cracking, plus power seat, sunroof, rear hatch glass and third-row function.
what_would_change_verdict: Photographed invoices for the 179k timing belt/water pump/radiator plus the 162k-173k suspension work, with dates and shop names, would move documentation and condition up sharply and justify most of the asking price.
A clean specialist PPI showing healthy rear air suspension (or a documented quality coil conversion), no stored codes, dry engine and a rust-free frame would make this a strong capability buy.
VIN release confirming a 2007 build, clean title and no reported accidents removes the identity question entirely.
Discovery of sagging/leaking rear bags, a masked AVS light, an oil leak at the rear main, or evidence of hard off-road use under the skid plates would push this down and out at $14,000.
Seller declining a PPI or refusing the VIN would end it regardless of how good the photos look.
evidence.mission_note: This is a legitimate utility_capability candidate: body-on-frame, full-time 4WD, V8, roof basket and flat cargo floor give Jason camping and trail capability the RX 350 genuinely cannot supply, and Corona is an easy retrieval. But it duplicates the RX for family/dog duty, so it only earns the driveway spot if the off-pavement and rooftop-tent use is actually wanted — and it does nothing for the enthusiast brief, so it does not substitute for the MINI/GTI/Z3 search.
evidence.rationale: The single most valuable thing in this ad — timing belt, water pump and radiator done at 179k, i.e. 19,500 miles ago — is exactly the claim that must not be taken on trust, and the seller supplied no dates, no shop names and no receipts for it or for the other seven jobs. What the photographs do establish is good: straight black paint with even gaps, clean rockers and arches on a Southern California truck, grey leather with only light wear, four matching deep-tread 33in BFGs on matching Method wheels plus a full-size matching spare, and a level unsagged stance on a quality Eibach Pro-Truck kit rather than a cheap spacer lift. What they do not show is anything that matters mechanically at 198,500 miles: no engine bay, no undercarriage or frame, no odometer, no instrument cluster, and no mention anywhere of the rear air springs or height-control system despite a lift having been installed — the second of the profile's two biggest price drivers is simply absent from the conversation. The listing also contradicts itself on year, headline 2008 versus the seller's own '2007 NOT a 2008', and there is no VIN to settle it or to pull a history report. On price, $14,000 asks more than the 195k-mile Oceanside car that sold at $13,000 and well more than the 192k-mile Sport that stalled at $11,600, and the profile warns that modified builds discount rather than premium against clean stock examples. Hazed headlights are the only defect the evidence actually establishes. The seller reads cooperative — he corrected his own year, he has a long-standing profile, and he is buying a GX550, which is a coherent reason to sell — so the fix here is cheap: VIN, receipt photos, a scan, and a specialist PPI.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN plus photographed invoices for the 179k timing belt/water pump/radiator, and ask directly whether the rear air bags are original, replaced or coil-converted — then, if those answers hold, book a Toyota/Lexus specialist PPI near Corona before traveling.

highlights: Timing belt and radiator replaced at 106K with receipts
CA vehicle its entire life, clean title
OME lift and 4x4 Labs bumper for light off-road use
Multiple driveline/cooling upgrades documented
red_flags: High mileage at 171,000 with no full maintenance history provided
normalized.prelim_summary: This 2003 Lexus GX470 sold for $15,500 with 171,000 miles, a clean CA title, documented timing belt/radiator service, and several off-road-oriented upgrades like an OME lift and aftermarket bumper. Seller claims good frame condition but no photos or third-party inspection are mentioned.

documentation.why: Seller states timing belt/radiator done at 106K with receipts, plus specific mod list, but no photos or VIN shown.

condition.why: Clean CA title, frame stated clean, receipts for timing belt/radiator, new tires cited; no independent inspection or photos of underside.

spec.why: OME lift, 4x4 Labs bumper and driveline upgrades add desirability, but base trim GX470 with high mileage.
